<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **29** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/system.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/translation.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**8** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/object-extensions.mdx`  _(via relatedLists (literal, a string literal in getPackagedObjectBase))_
- `content/docs/deployment/environment-variables.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/plugins/adding-a-metadata-type.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/i18n-standard.mdx`  _(via relatedLists (literal, a string literal in getPackagedObjectBase))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/plugin-spec.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/ui/pages.mdx`  _(via relatedLists (literal, a string literal in getPackagedObjectBase))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-4.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`  _(via relatedLists (literal, a string literal in getPackagedObjectBase))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/system.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/translation.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **68** of **251** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **178** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 84853fd18eb28a5481415c2d698d04025aa629e1` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `3d4ed3cb7db98f51c3c00465d9568acba5722dad` — the merge of head `6fd5bb8573ec4fbcdb37772a5e6aabbf48871b17` into base `84853fd18eb28a5481415c2d698d04025aa629e1`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 3d4ed3cb7db98f51c3c00465d9568acba5722dad && git checkout 3d4ed3cb7db98f51c3c00465d9568acba5722dad
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 84853fd18eb28a5481415c2d698d04025aa629e1 6fd5bb8573ec4fbcdb37772a5e6aabbf48871b17 && git checkout -B drift-repro 84853fd18eb28a5481415c2d698d04025aa629e1 && git merge --no-ff 6fd5bb8573ec4fbcdb37772a5e6aabbf48871b17

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 84853fd18eb28a5481415c2d698d04025aa629e1
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 84853fd18eb28a5481415c2d698d04025aa629e1` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `4249fe4ba842b1a047bc9c9e68dbce5ce0dae0f2`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts, packages/spec/src/system/translation.zod.ts + packages/lint/src/i18n-walk.ts, packages/lint/src/object-graph.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-translation-references.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-translated-echo.ts

Read: card #36528 (body and its 3 comments: triage, claim, dev report), PR #36574 (body, 18-file list, net diff against merge-base `65ce7983`), the 47 check-runs on the head. Code outside the diff was read at the head, never reviewed: `packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts`, `packages/spec/src/data/related-list-entry.ts`, `packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-read-decorations.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/registry-platform-global.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/registry-custom-arrangement.ts`, `packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts`, `ui/packages/app-shell/src/utils/deriveRelatedLists.ts`. Everything below is derived by reading; nothing was run.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept-set, `ObjectTranslationDataSchema`: gains `_relatedLists`, a record of closed leaves with the one key `label`. Right as a widening: the parent schema is a strict object, so the key was refused as unknown before and is accepted now; no other key's verdict moves, and every other unknown key is refused as before. The un-prefixed `relatedLists` gains an alias row onto `_relatedLists`: it was refused before and is still refused, now with the rename named. Right.
- Key shape (check a): `_relatedLists` sits beside `_views`, `_actions`, `_sections`, `_tabs`, `_validations` and follows their spelling (the authoring key with the underscore prefix, plus the un-prefixed alias). It does not collide with a read decoration: `METADATA_READ_DECORATIONS` is an exact-name list (`_diagnostics`, `_draft`, `_withheldFields`, `_relatedListsArrangement`) stripped from served metadata documents, and this key lives in translation data, where its siblings already carry the prefix. LIST is the entry's literal `list`, the same spelling `RelatedListEntryObjectSchema.list` takes (child object, or object.field as one key); the built-in tabs cannot be object-form entries, so they have no key. The slot it overrides is the entry's own `label` (`z.string().min(1).optional()` on `main`), which the console reads at `deriveRelatedLists.ts:657`. Right.
- Public surface, `translateObject`: one more overlaid slot on the served object (`relatedLists[].label` of a labelled object-form entry). It maps existing entries only: a key for a list with no entry is dropped, no entry is created, the array reference is kept when nothing matched, `_relatedListsArrangement` is untouched, so which tabs show and their order cannot change. Right for the object's own entries. Wrong for an entry a code package's `place` brings, on the read the REST exit actually makes: see M1.
- Lint accept-set: `translation-target-unknown` gains a `_relatedLists` leg through the shared `orphan` helper, severity `error` as its siblings (pinned in the lane's test). Right for the object's own entries; over-accepts for `place`-brought entries: see M1.
- `VisibleObjectExtension` (lint, internal fold shape) gains `relatedListEntries`. Additive; right.
- Echo restore: one more restored slot, matched by `list`, with the existing advisory. Right (④, check d).
- Generated surface agrees with the zod: `authorable-surface/system.json` gains `system/ObjectTranslationData:_relatedLists`; `content/docs/references/system/translation.mdx` gains the row in each of the five object-translation tables and the nested shape; the strictness-ledger count moves 408 to 409 for the one new strict site. Nothing previously accepted is refused.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/36528-related-list-label-translation.md`: `minor` on `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`. That matches what the diff publishes: an additive authorable key and an additive overlay (spec), an additive rule leg and walk entry (lint), an additive restored slot (metadata-protocol). `@objectstack/objectql` gains a test file only and needs no entry. The `Check Changeset` run on the head concluded success.

Clause-②: yes (widening), on the PR body and the changeset. The declaration is the lane's; as a judgment of the diff, nothing narrows.

`Metadata-protocol: added` is on both; `Skills-docs: follow-up owed` names the two skill files.

One sentence of the changeset is not true of the head and is published text: "A labelled entry an object extension brings (a list placement in `place`, ...) ... its key resolves and is translated too." For `place` it is not translated on the REST read (M1). It moves with M1's fix.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev deviation, files outside the claim's File surface (`packages/lint/src/object-graph.ts`, two lint meta-tests, the objectql pin test, `packages/spec/liveness/translation.json`): `object-graph.ts` is the fold the orphan rule reads and is reviewed here as an implementing file; the rest are the lane's ACCEPT. Answered.
- Dev deviation, worktree branch pushed as `claude/project-thread-qwdwll`: process only. Answered.
- Acceptance note "the extractor walk does not read `objectExtensions`": true at the head (`collectExpectedEntries` reads `obj.relatedLists` only) and the same gap fields have. Accepted as pre-existing; it bears on M1 only in that nothing scaffolds the key M1 is about.
- Acceptance note "a `place` entry's label applies only where the extended object declares `relatedLists`; the orphan rule accepts its key regardless": answered by M1, which is the stronger form of it.
- Acceptance note "the echo restore does not restore `listViews` copy or `validations[].message`": pre-existing and outside this diff; a follow-up card, not this PR's.
- `open_questions`: the dev report carries none.
- Serial constraint #36517: merged; the merge-base `65ce7983` carries it, and the diff builds on its fold.
- SQL push-down: the diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join; every change is over in-memory documents. Nothing to flag.
- Check-runs on the head, read 2026-11-23: completed with success: `Check Changeset`, `Spec property liveness`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check PR Size`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `PR-body guards`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Plan Test Core shards`, `Plan Test UI shards`, `filter`, `Auto Label`. Skipped by their own conditions: 8 (queue verdicts, opt-in harnesses, dogfood shards). PENDING, not waited for: `Test Core` 1/10 to 10/10, `Build Core`, `Build Docs`, `Build UI Deps`, `Live E2E UI`, the four `Type Check` runs, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus`, `Lint · scoped · query-options erasure`. None has failed. The dev's own 118-command claim is not a gate verdict and is not adopted.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/system/translation.zod.ts`.** The key holds against the claim comment's naming call and its first consumer: a closed leaf, `label` only, keyed by a free string (the dotted `event.related_to` is one record key, which the resolver indexes directly and never splits). The docblock's sentences are true of `translateObjectRelatedLists` for an object's own entries: only an authored label is translated, nothing is swapped in for an entry without one, built-in tabs have no key.

**`packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts`.** `translateObjectRelatedLists` is a faithful twin of `translateObjectListViews`: same early return, same `valueOverridesPackagedBase` comparison (no second copy), same three edges (no base: catalog applies; base without the entry: diverged; base with the same label: catalog applies), same-reference return. Locale chain as `_tabs`. An empty or equal translation leaves the entry alone. For the object's own entries, a tenant rewrite and a `.custom` arrangement's relabel, this is the ADR-0029 D9.2a / ADR-0146 D2 order and it is right. The break is at the one case the PR adds on top of the card:

M1 (must-fix) — A tab title a CODE package's `place` brings is not translated on the real read, while the lint rule, three docblocks, the changeset and the PR body say it is. Trace at the head: the registry fold splices `place: [{ list, after, label }]` into the served parent's `relatedLists` as `{ list, label }`. The REST read exit (`packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts`, both the list and the single-item path) hands `translateObject` `packagedBase = getPackagedObjectBase(name)`, which is the OWNER's declaration before the fold (`registry-platform-global.ts`: it adds only code extenders' `validations` and added `fields`; `relatedLists` stays the owner's, and the `TranslateDocumentOptions.packagedBase` docblock says the same). In `translateObjectRelatedLists` the base is then known and carries no entry for the placed list, so `packagedEntry` is `{}`, `valueOverridesPackagedBase({}, 'label', label)` is true, and the label reads `catalogs.changed`: the base's paired `.custom` bundle, or nothing. The deployment catalog, where the placing package's own `objects.TARGET._relatedLists.LIST.label` lands, is never asked. A `place` label applies only where the target declares `relatedLists`, so the base's array is always present in that case and this is the only outcome. Consequences in the reviewed files: (1) `validate-translation-references.ts` accepts that key as resolving (extension-fold leg, and the docblock sentence "the served target carries that entry, which `translateObject` translates as it does the target's own" plus the "FOUR of this rule's rungs are reachable through an extension" paragraph), so `os validate` is green on a key no served read uses, the false-green the orphan rule exists to prevent; (2) `object-graph.ts` carries `place` entries for that reader on the same premise; (3) the changeset and PR body publish "translated too". The lane's pin, `packages/objectql/src/registry-related-lists-label-translation-36528.test.ts`, calls `translateObject(served, BUNDLE, { locale })` with no `packagedBase`, which is not the read's option set, so it is green on a path production does not take. The same shape was already solved twice for fields: a field a code extender adds is carried into the packaged base (`packagedAddedFields`, the #27559 principle), and a patched slot reads its package's bundle (`patchBundles`, #33952). Two fixes close it; the lane picks one. (a) Make it true: `getPackagedObjectBase` carries the list entries code extenders place, as it carries their added fields, so the placed label compares equal and the catalog applies; pin it through the read's real options (with `packagedBase` from the registry), and the echo restore then follows for free because it translates with the same base. (b) Make the claim match the code: the orphan rule stops accepting a `place`-brought key (a `.custom` arrangement's stays, it reads the pair's bundle by design), the docblocks, changeset and PR body drop "place", the pin is either removed or given the real options, and the gap gets a follow-up card. The `.custom` arrangement half of the same claim holds: its label is diverged by design and reads the pair's own translations, which is ADR-0146 D2's first rank.

**`packages/lint/src/i18n-walk.ts`.** `pushRelatedListLabels` emits exactly the entries the resolver overlays (object-form, string `list`, non-empty string `label`), the dotted list as one path segment, seeded from the label. Agrees with the contract.

**`packages/lint/src/validate-translation-references.ts`.** For an object's own entries the leg is right: it resolves over labelled entries only, flags a ghost name with a suggestion, and gives the named-but-unlabelled case its own verdict; an object with no `relatedLists` flags every key. Beyond M1:

N1 (nit) — The named-but-unlabelled hint, "Give the entry a `label` ({ list, label }) ... or translate the child lookup field's `relatedListTitle`", is also what a key over a bare built-in tab (`sys_attachment`, `sys_approval_request`, `sys_activity`) gets, and for those the schema refuses the object form and there is no child field. The flag is right; only the prescription misleads, for a key few will write.

N2 (nit) — The extension leg adds a `.custom` entry's `list` to the labelled set whenever it has a `label`, `{ list, hidden: true, label }` included. The registry fold drops hidden entries from the served list, so a key over one resolves nothing and is not flagged. Permissive, and narrow.

N3 (nit) — A finding's path prints a dotted list unbracketed (`..._relatedLists.event.related_to`) where the locale segment is bracketed (`["zh-CN"]`), so the path reads as two segments. Display only.

**`packages/lint/src/object-graph.ts`.** The fold's new `relatedListEntries` filters to record entries of `relatedLists` and `place`; a field or group placement has no `list` and is skipped by the reader. Sound as a carrier; its `place` half serves the claim M1 refutes and moves with M1's fix.

**`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-translated-echo.ts`** (check d). The stored source's `relatedLists` is put on the stored document, each locale's read is made with the read's own options (the same `packagedBase`), and an incoming entry label is put back only when some read of the source translates the source label to exactly it and the two differ; an author's own title, and a title on an entry the source leaves untitled, are kept (`NOT_DECLARED`). Entries are matched by `list`, the array is copied only on a hit, other entries and `columns` are untouched. Patch and injected sources declare no `relatedLists`, so they answer nothing here. A translated read written back therefore stores the source title: round-trip safe. Agrees with the contract sentence added to the module header.

## Contract review

### ① Derived judgments

- Unchanged since the first record and still right: the `ObjectTranslationDataSchema._relatedLists` accept-set (a widening; closed leaf, `label` only, the `relatedLists` alias row), the `translateObject` overlay, the walk entry, the echo slot, the generated surface. The two hits files, `i18n-walk.ts`, `object-graph.ts` and `protocol-translated-echo.ts` carry no round-2 change.
- Public surface, `SchemaRegistry#getPackagedObjectBase` (new in this round): the answer's `relatedLists` now carries the entries an enabled CODE extender's `place` splices into the owner's declared tab list. Additive on a read: nothing an author could write is refused, and the answer is the owner's definition by reference exactly as before when no code extender ships a rule, adds a field or places a list. Right.
